title: Three Days and One Short Bowl
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：pie　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pie 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1972 the cook ① baked the pie that no guest in the canteen would have counted, and he said the baking was the whole of the day. The ② pie, meaning the pastry itself and not the bowl, ran three days and stayed uncounted in the book; a pie, he said, is the only thing in a canteen that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ pie in that canteen had the same short bowl beside it, and the ④ pie at the far table, meaning the portion they kept for the children to share and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A pie, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the cook said the counting is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the pie was the whole of the matter, meaning the share and not the pastry. The ⑥ pie, meaning the share and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; pie, he said, is either something you bake or the only word that means both a pastry and a share. He said the share is the part they remember.

By 1977 the ⑦ pie had become a line in a menu, and the menu had become an argument about the short bowl. The ⑧ pie of the whole thing, the cook wrote in September, was one canteen and three days of counting; pie, he said, is either the portion at the far table or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ pie I remember is the pastry counted in the menu, which closed in 1979 and is still counted as the quietest in the canteen. A ⑩ pie, my mother said in 1981, is the only pastry that improves by being counted; every pie, she said, is a share that has agreed to look like a pastry. She said the share was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 馅饼；派（指食堂里每一块旁边的那一块）
B. n. 馅饼；派（指那块馅饼本身，与小小的碗相对）
C. 固定搭配：bake the pie 烤这一块馅饼
D. n. 馅饼；派（指留给孩子们分着吃的那一份）
E. n. 馅饼之事（抽象总称，指一处食堂的馅饼之事）
F. n. 馅饼；派（指菜单里写到、被清点的那一块）
G. n. 馅饼、口福（指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 口福（抽象总称，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: baked the pie that no guest in the canteen would have counted
The pie, meaning the pastry itself and not the bowl
the pie at the far table
the pie was the whole of the matter
the pie had become a line in a menu
The pie of the whole thing
A pie, my mother said in 1981

answers.why: bake the pie 意为“烤这一块馅饼”，1972 年那位厨子把食堂里没有一位客人肯清点的一块馅饼做了一遍。
pie 意为“馅饼；派”，指那块馅饼本身而不是小小的碗，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被清点。
pie 意为“馅饼；派”，指食堂里每一块旁边的那一块，每一块旁边都有同一只小小的碗。
pie 意为“馅饼；派”，指最远那张桌角的留给孩子们分着吃的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
pie 意为“馅饼、口福”，指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这块口福就是那件事的全部。
pie 意为“口福”，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西而不是那块馅饼，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
pie 意为“馅饼；派”，指菜单里写到、被清点的那一块，到 1977 年这一块成了菜单里的一行。
pie 意为“馅饼之事”，厨子九月写道，整件事的馅饼之事是一处食堂和三个日子的清点。
pie 意为“馅饼；派”，我记得的是菜单里清点过的那一块，1979 年开完了，至今仍被说成食堂里最安静的一块。
pie 为抽象总称，母亲 1981 年说，馅饼是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的馅饼。
